claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology is a collaboration between the Center for Open Science and Science Exchange that seeks to address concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology (RP:CB) is a collaboration between the Center for Open Science and Science Exchange that seeks to address concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology (Errington et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Errington et al., 2014 describing the RP:CB project.

claim: For each paper in the Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology, a Registered Report detailing the proposed experimental designs and protocols for the replications was peer reviewed and published prior to data collection.
source: For each of these papers a Registered Report detailing the proposed experimental designs and protocols for the replications was peer reviewed and published prior to data collection.
evidence: Describes the methodology of the RP:CB project.

claim: Many cancers contain a subset of cells, termed cancer stem cells (CSCs), that are less differentiated and contribute to tumor progression and metastasis in various cancers.
source: Many cancers contain a subset of cells, termed cancer stem cells (CSCs), that are less differentiated and contribute to tumor progression and metastasis in various cancers (Kim et al., 2018; Takayama et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kim et al., 2018 and Takayama et al., 2017.
